info.title: Acta API
info.description: Acta's operator API, the one the dashboard uses. Lists page by cursor: pass a page's nextCursor back as cursor until hasMore is false; a cursor is tied to its query. Every POST, PUT, and DELETE is a control, mapped only where the host enables controls, and where the host requires it the call carries the confirmation header the operation lists, with the value true. A control whose request object is optional acts with its defaults when the request has no body; one that declares application/json and sends no bytes answers 400, so send {} or leave the content type off. A signal raise takes any JSON value instead, and no bytes, with or without the content type, raise a presence-only signal. POST /jobs answers 201 when it inserted the job and 200 when a deduplication key matched an existing one, with the job's URL in Location either way. A string carrying x-acta-known-values is an open set: compare against the known values and keep any other value as it is. The document declares no security scheme: the host adds its own authentication, which a client sends as the host asks.

AlertDeliveryStatusCode.description:
Delivery state of one alert row. Numeric bands are a readability convention only; behavior follows the explicit members.

Known values:
- unspecified: Alert delivery status not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- pending: Materialized; awaiting the first send attempt.
- retry-after: Send deferred until the alert's retry_after_utc instant.
- suppressed: Intentionally not sent because process-local channel policy rejected delivery.
- delivered: Successfully sent to the channel transport.
- failed: Send attempt failed and the retry path is done with it; re-sent as a reminder while the incident stays unresolved.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

AlertKindCode.description:

Known values:
- unspecified: Alert kind not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- first-failure: Failure that opened the incident; emitted by Automatic origin on non-terminal failure.
- threshold-reached: Threshold-bound emission (e.g., LostClaimAlertThreshold reached).
- final-failure: Terminal failure; emitted by Automatic origin on Status to Failed.
- manual: Hand-raised; ctx.AlertAsync from inside a handler.

AlertOriginCode.description:

Known values:
- unspecified: Alert origin not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- automatic: System-emitted from a state-mutating SP (failure / timeout / orphan / deadline).
- manual: ctx.AlertAsync from inside a user handler.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

AlertProfileCode.description:
When the engine raises alerts for a definition's jobs on its own.

Known values:
- none: No automatic failure alerts. ctx.AlertAsync still creates rows.
- on-failure: Default. Alerts on every failed or orphaned attempt; repeats collapse onto the job's one open incident. Final exhaustion writes a separate alert (a different reason yields a different DeduplicationKey). Every enabled profile records the attempts its alerts read whatever the event recording level, so an alert never depends on recording. Resolves on recovery, the job's next success.
- info: Informational alerts on terminal failure only; low severity. A recurring slot rarely reaches one - see on-terminal. Resolves on recovery, the job's next success.
- on-terminal: Alert on terminal failure only: retry budget exhausted, ctx.FailAsync, a non-retryable exception, or an interrupted at-most-once step, or a lost lease that spent the budget. Resolves on recovery, the job's next success. A deadline lands the job Cancelled rather than Failed and so alerts under no profile. A recurring slot never exhausts a budget and re-arms after an unhandled exception or a lost lease, so use on-failure to hear about those.
- sys-critical: Reserved for system Jobs. Emits at Severity = Critical to the Job's channel, or the configured "default" channel when none is declared.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

AlertRef.description: Public stable reference for one alert row: "alr_" plus the Guid's 32 lowercase hex digits, such as alr_01a14f5038c17d0e9b2f6a4c81d3e5f7. Dashboards, HTTP APIs, and alert transports address alerts by this value; the numeric alert id stays the internal engine identity. Deduplication never re-mints it: a condition that re-fires while its incident is open keeps that incident's ref.

AlertSeverityCode.description:
How severe an alert is.

Known values:
- unspecified: Alert severity not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- info: Informational; not paging.
- warning: Non-terminal failure transition; repeats collapse onto the one open incident.
- error: Terminal failure or operator-attention event.
- critical: Highest severity; emitted by system Jobs (AlertProfile = SysCritical) and operator alerts for incidents. Whether it pages depends on the routed channel's transport and config.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

- progress: Progress; UPSERT, last-writer-wins, one per job.

CheckpointStatusCode.description:
Where a checkpoint that has a status stands. A signal or child latch is pending until it is set or its wait expires; a timer is pending until it is consumed; a firing is pending until it succeeds, fails, or is cancelled. Variables and progress have no status.

- expired: The re-entering wait found the checkpoint overdue and settled it TimedOut; a raise then skips it.
- consumed: Due instant reached; the replayed handler consumed the timer and proceeded.
- succeeded: The firing settled successfully; the envelope is the slot's last outcome until the next admission replaces it.
- failed: The firing settled as a final failure; the envelope is the slot's last outcome until the next admission replaces it.
- cancelled: The firing settled by cancellation; the envelope is the slot's last outcome until the next admission replaces it.

EventCode.description:
What an event records, as a dotted code. There is no code for an enqueue, because the job row itself records it.

- tenant.suspended: An operator suspended a tenant; the name stops resolving at enqueue. EventMessage carries the reason.
- tenant.resumed: An operator resumed a suspended tenant; its key resolves at enqueue again. EventMessage carries the reason.
- tenant.updated: An operator changed a tenant display name / description. EventMessage carries the reason.
- namespace.suspended: An operator suspended a namespace; enqueue into it is rejected. EventMessage carries the reason.
- namespace.resumed: An operator resumed a suspended namespace; enqueue into it is allowed again. EventMessage carries the reason.
- namespace.updated: An operator changed a namespace owner team / description. EventMessage carries the reason.
- definition.overrides-updated: An operator changed a job definition's policy overrides; EventMessage summarizes the change.
- definition.retired: An operator retired a job definition; enqueue is rejected and its parked jobs were cancelled.
- job.execution-succeeded: The attempt's handler returned successfully; DurationMs is set. Audit records every one, Failures a success after counted failures, and an enabled alert profile also a one-shot's success past its first attempt.
- job.execution-failed: The attempt failed and the job lives on: a retry within budget, or a recurring job's firing that spent its budget and returned the slot to Idle. DurationMs and the failure's EventMessage are set; details carry reason and to.
- job.execution-orphaned: The attempt's worker lease expired and crash recovery reclaimed the job without ending it. WorkerId names the stale holder; details carry reason and to.
- job.execution-yielded: The attempt ended without succeeding or failing: rescheduled, suspended, paused, or cancelled by its handler or the engine. Audit only; details carry outcome and reason.
- job.failed: The job failed for good: its retry budget is spent, its handler failed it, or its failure is not retryable. DurationMs is set when an attempt ran; details carry reason.
- job.suspended: The attempt parked on a durable wait: a ctx.SleepAsync timer re-armed the job Ready at its due instant, or a signal or child wait left it Suspended. Budget-neutral; details carry to.
- job.rescheduled: The job re-armed Ready with a new NextRunAtUtc: a handler reschedule, a failed attempt's retry within budget, or an operator RescheduleAsync; details carry actor or reason.
- job.cancelled: Job was cancelled (Status to Cancelled, terminal).
- job.paused: Job was paused (Status to Paused).
- job.resumed: Job was resumed (Status to Ready).
- job.restarted: Job was restarted (Status to Ready; failure_count reset, retention cleared, execution_number unchanged).
- job.reprioritized: Operator changed the job's claim priority; EventMessage carries the operator's reason, if any.
- job.purged: Operator hard-deleted a terminal job; the subject is the deleted job's id. Details snapshot its jobRef, correlationKey, and actor. Always emitted regardless of event recording.
- job.input-amended: Operator amended a job's stored input payload; details carry the actor and bounded metadata (format name and byte count) about the previous payload, and EventMessage carries the why.
- job.signal-raised: Signal delivered via IJobs.RaiseSignalAsync; matching signal checkpoint (State = Set) UPSERTed.
- job.state-reset: Handler called ctx.ResetStateAsync; the job's checkpoints and steps were cleared so the next execution starts as new. The scheduler's firing envelope stays.
- job.note-recorded: Application-authored note from ctx.NoteAsync. The only event code an application can write and one the runtime never emits, so every other event stays provably system-written. EventMessage carries the line; details carry the optional payload.
- schedule.paused: A recurring schedule was paused; details carry the schedule name.
- schedule.resumed: A recurring schedule was resumed; details carry the schedule name.
- schedule.pause-expired: A timed pause elapsed; the scheduler auto-resumed the schedule. Details carry the schedule name.
- schedule.triggered: Operator admitted a manual firing of the slot; no schedule cursor moved. Details carry the schedule name.
- schedule.admitted: The admission engine selected one of the schedule's occurrences for a firing; details carry the schedule, the occurrence, the covered-through boundary, and the firing id.
- schedule.skipped: A range of the schedule's occurrences was decided without work: the misfire policy skipped it, it expired, the schedule was full, its calendar no longer produces it, or a calendar publication discarded it; details carry the schedule, the range, and the reason.
- schedule.retimed: A deploy changed the schedule's timing, or a calendar it names was published; the undecided occurrences of the old timing were discarded and the cursor moved to the first occurrence of the new one. Details carry the schedule name.
- calendar.draft-saved: An operator saved a new draft version of a catalog calendar. Details carry the calendar, the version, and the role; EventMessage carries the reason.
- calendar.published: An operator published a catalog calendar version, which became the family's current one. Details carry the calendar, the version, the version it replaced, the overdue decision, and the schedules it affected.
- calendar.archived: An operator archived a catalog calendar's current version; the family has no current version until another is published. Details carry the calendar and the version.
- worker.started: Worker process registered; a workers row was appended (Status: Active).
- worker.stopped: Worker process shut down cleanly (Status: Active/Draining to Stopped).
- worker.died: Worker heartbeat went stale; crash recovery flipped the worker to Dead.
- alert.acknowledged: Operator acknowledged an alert; EventMessage carries the note.
- alert.resolved: Operator manually resolved an alert; EventMessage carries the note.
- outbox.requeued: An operator command returned quarantined outbox rows to Pending; EventMessage carries the justification and the row ids.
- outbox.discarded: An operator command deleted quarantined outbox rows; EventMessage carries the justification and the deleted row ids.

JobKindCode.description:
What a jobs row is: an ordinary job, or the one permanent slot a scheduled definition fires through. The kind is written at insert and never changes; the executor and the operator verbs read it instead of guessing from a deduplication key or from the schedules a row happens to own.

Known values:
- unspecified: Job kind not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- ordinary: A job enqueued by an application, an operator, or a parent handler, or admitted by a schedule as a per-occurrence root; it ends in a terminal status.
- permanent-slot: The one reusable job of a scheduled definition; registration creates it, every firing of the definition's schedules runs through it, and it is never terminal by itself.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

json.description: A JSON payload, embedded as the JSON value itself: any JSON value, null included.

formatId.description: The payload format's id. Beside base64 it is required: 2 for bytes, or 128 to 255 for an application's own. Beside json it is left out, or is 1.

JobPriorityCode.description:
A job's priority. A worker always claims the highest priority first, with no aging, so keep bulk work in a namespace of its own.

Known values:
- bulk: Lowest practical priority; bulk-class workloads.
- normal: Default priority. Most jobs use this.
- high: Above normal; operator opt-in for time-sensitive work.
- critical: Critical priority; close-to-realtime operator workloads.
- realtime: Highest priority.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

JobRef.description: Public stable reference for one Job row: "job_" plus the Guid's 32 lowercase hex digits, such as job_01a14f4e954e7bf68ac609f3fcad8e3d. Dashboards, HTTP APIs, and clients address jobs by this value; the numeric JobId stays the internal engine identity. It copies and searches as one word, and a UUIDv7 reads in creation order.

JobStatusCode.description:
Where a job is in its life.

Known values:
- unspecified: Job status not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- ready: Eligible for claim; the claim path selects rows in this Status.
- blocked: Waiting behind an earlier unfinished job of its lane; the claim never offers it, and the settle of the job ahead promotes it to Ready.
- suspended: Parked and not progressing: awaiting an external signal via ctx.WaitSignalAsync, or awaiting children via ctx.WaitChildAsync / WaitChildrenAsync.
- paused: Not running, awaiting an external trigger to resume.
- idle: A permanent slot between firings: no outstanding firing, no lease, no claim time. Admission makes it Ready; it is never terminal.
- executing: Claimed by a worker under a live lease; its handler is running or about to start.
- succeeded: Terminal success.
- failed: Terminal failure: MaxAttempts exhausted, a non-retryable exception, an interrupted at-most-once step, or ctx.FailAsync.
- cancelled: Terminal cancellation by IJobs.CancelAsync or ctx.Cancel.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

MisfireStrategyCode.description:
What a schedule does about occurrences it missed during downtime.

Known values:
- unspecified: Misfire strategy not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- catch-up-once: After downtime, fire once immediately for all missed occurrences, then resume from the next occurrence after now.
- skip: After downtime, skip all missed occurrences and resume from the first occurrence strictly after now.
- catch-up-latest: After downtime, fire once for the latest missed occurrence, the earlier ones coalesced into it, then resume from the next occurrence after now.
- catch-up-all: After downtime, fire every missed occurrence in order, one per settlement, subject to the schedule's capacity.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

NamespaceStatusCode.description:
Namespace state machine. 10-spaced ids; live states 10..80, mirroring TenantStatusCode.

Known values:
- unspecified: Namespace status not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- active: Namespace resolves at enqueue; enqueue allowed.
- suspended: Enqueue into the namespace is rejected and its schedules hold. Reversible (operator hold). Existing in-flight jobs are unaffected.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

OverdueDecisionCode.description:
What a calendar publication does with the occurrences a dependent schedule has not decided yet that are already due under the version it replaces.

Known values:
- unspecified: Overdue decision not recognized by this build; the value was written by a newer Acta.
